title: How Well Do LLMs Represent Values Across Cultures? Empirical Analysis of LLM Responses Based on Hofstede Cultural Dimensions

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs with advice-seeking scenarios requiring a binary choice between opposite ends of Hofstede's cultural dimensions (e.g., Individualism vs. Collectivism), and measuring the correlation between the model's choices and the expected cultural values of 36 different country personas.

Translating advice prompts into 36 languages (categorized as high, mid, and low-resource) to evaluate whether an LLM's ability to align with specific cultural values differs based on the language's resource availability and training data representation.

Qualitatively analyzing LLM justifications for their advice to identify the presence of national stereotypes, misrepresentations, and hallucinations (e.g., assuming a Russian persona drinks vodka or using inaccurate regional idioms) when prompted to act as a specific country's citizen.
